api.notes: A theme name, or an object with a name (also the theme attribute, as a string). Only the name is used until core/theme (WP-1) wires a DefinedTheme to it.

hooks.notes: @tecton-wc/core/context/keys.js: {name, mode}, mode already resolved to light or dark.
Consume themeContext with a ContextConsumer for name and resolved mode; read token values with getComputedStyle(host).getPropertyValue(). The upstream token() resolver arrives with core/theme (WP-1).
Theme used it to resolve system mode; tct-theme listens to (prefers-color-scheme: dark) itself and only while system mode is live.

differences.text: Only the theme name is used. Runtime defineTheme() token overrides, component overrides and style injection belong to core/theme (WP-1), which wires a DefinedTheme to the theme property; the Tecton token set comes from tokens.css.

The wrapper is a block that paints the page surface (--color-background-body) and text colour, not display: contents (theme-island rule, A§8.1), so a nested island is visible on its own. It uses the token blocks keyed by data-theme; data-astryx-theme is data-tct-theme.

The root synchronisation also restores the previous <html data-theme> and data-tct-theme values when the last root theme disconnects (upstream removed them), and several roots do not fight: the first owns <html> and the next takes over when it leaves.

mode is reflected and drives the island's color-scheme through attribute selectors, and system inside a forced island follows the operating system (color-scheme: light dark), as upstream's system class did.

core.theme.notes: Guides: [mwg:dark-mode] color-scheme on the root through data-theme, system default, media-query change listener; [mwg:component-specific-light-dark-theme] color-scheme on an island so light-dark() tokens resolve per subtree; [mwg:custom-elements] provider without a shadow root; [mwg:styling-web-components] light-DOM sheet adopted once per root.
